basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 24.' and it opens '| Vers. 24. Sedit in forti arcus ejus. Id est, virtus ejus et spes ejus sedit, hoc est'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: | Vers. 24. Sedit in forti arcus ejus. Id est, virtus ejus et spes ejus sedit, hoc est stabilita est in forti, hoc est in Christo. Et dissoluta sunt vincula brachiorum ejus per manus potentis Jacob, id est omnipotentis Dei. Inde, id est ex Jacob progenie, egressus est lapis, id est Christus; egressus est pastor, id est Christus, qui est et lapis Israel, id est firmitas et robur omnium Deum contemplantium.
